subject: AuroraHealth capacity runway & quality economics note
messages:
From: Melanie Ortiz <melanie.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Usage review ahead of renewal — capacity and quality concerns

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the check-in last week. We dove into our November usage and wanted a clear read before the renewal:

- Token spend is up ~38% month-over-month vs Sept baseline, driven by a burst in summarization traffic.
- We're seeing intermittent tail latency for long-context batches (p90 jumped from 420ms to ~1.2s during peak windows). That is triggering our internal alerting.
- Our product team is asking whether we should increase committed capacity for Q1 and/or change the billing term so we can lock in a lower unit rate.

Can you send a short ROI recap that shows: current token economics, expected cost delta for a 20% committed increase vs burst credits, and any notes on model/quantization options that might reduce unit cost without sacrificing our quality thresholds?

I've attached a CSV with the raw usage slices by route so you can slice it by model and seq length. Also copied contracts — if there's a straightforward term amendment we can review, please include that.

Melanie
Melanie Ortiz
Head of Integrations, AuroraHealth
melanie.ortiz@aurorahealth.com
Attachment: aurora_usage_report_nov2026.csv (CSV, 98KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Melanie Ortiz <melanie.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, contracts@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-19T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage review ahead of renewal — capacity and quality concerns

Melanie — thanks for the data and the clear ask. High-level summary attached (PDF) and TL;DR below.

TL;DR:
- Current blended token rate: $0.0009/token. Forecasted net spend (run-rate) at current usage: ~$103k/mo.
- Option A (20% committed increase, 12-month term): projected unit rate = $0.00081/token (10% discount), estimated monthly spend = ~$116k/mo but with 20% more committed units and lower overage risk.
- Option B (No commit, burst credits + on-demand autoscale): higher per-token ($0.00095) during bursts; recommended if you expect short-lived spikes only.
- Ops note: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant on non-critical summarization routes could cut inferred token compute cost ~18% with <1% measured quality delta on our evals.

Suggested next steps:
1) If you want predictability, Option A + a 30-day ramp (canary traffic split to the Dedicated pool) — we handle canary routing and fallbacks.
2) If you prefer flexibility, keep current commit and buy a 200k-token/month burst bucket for peak windows; we can auto-apply it when p95 latency exceeds 800ms.

I've attached the detailed worksheet (karthik_aurora_renewal_summary.pdf) with per-route economics and a proposed contract addendum language you can hand to contracts. Can we do a 30-minute sync Friday to finalize? I'm flexible 10–12 PT.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Attachment: karthik_aurora_renewal_summary.pdf (PDF, 310KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Internal — pricing + ops for Aurora options (AUR-2026-139)

Soojin / Ben — quick internal note after the external reply. Melanie is leaning toward predictability but will want assurance on latency for long-context summarization. A couple asks:

- Soojin: can you confirm Dedicated pool availability for a 20% uplift starting 2027-01-01 with a 30-day canary window? Also confirm we can enable prefix KV caching for their summarization routes; that should reduce p95 by ~30% in our sim.
- Ben: if we price Option A at a 10% unit discount vs current list, that puts the committed monthly at ~$116k — we should be comfortable approving a one-time onboarding credit of up to $6k to offset last month's tail-latency impact. Can legal/finance handle a short addendum that includes a one-month service credit?

I'll hold the Friday slot tentative but want to be ready with an addendum and a rollout plan.

—Karthik

From: Melanie Ortiz <melanie.ortiz@aurorahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@aurorahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-21T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage review ahead of renewal — capacity and quality concerns

Karthik — this is helpful, thank you. AuroraHealth is comfortable moving forward with Option A (20% committed increase, 12-month term) provided we include a one-month service credit to cover the latency windows we saw in November. If you can get that in the addendum and share DocuSign, we'll route for signatures today.

Also please include the quantization note in the rollout plan — product wants to trial the 4-bit variant on a single route for 30 days before broader conversion.

I'll have contracts follow-up on the exact sig block; attaching the signed addendum after signatures.

Best,
Melanie
Melanie Ortiz
Head of Integrations, AuroraHealth
Attachment: aurora_signed_addendum.pdf (PDF, 24KB)
